She's trying to act tough, all "leave me alone, this is inappropriate." All that proper white lady bullshit.
Her mouth is fighting. Her body ain't.
I can smell the fear on her, man. Every time I get close, she starts breathing all heavy, cheeks get all red. It's fucking delicious.
My hands curled into fists against the cold concrete. The blood rushed to my ears. I took a step forward, ready to round the corner.
(That sick fuck... I should walk out there and smash his teeth in right now.)
(And achieve what? A broken nose? Look at them. They’re twice your size.)
(Stay put, hero. If you jump in now, you lose the element of surprise. Listen.)
I forced myself to stay back, grinding my teeth.
Give her another week of this. She won't just be scared. She'll be begging me to tell her what to do, just to make it stop.
(And then she'll be begging him not to stop. Heh. The classic progression.)

s2_ntr_route_034.text: I walked into the general store, still trying to make sense of what I’d heard at the Dean's office. The grant... Darnell... it was all a mess. I grabbed a soda and walked to the counter to clear my head.
Rough day? You look like you just saw a murder.
Something like that. Just... ring it up, please.
The door chime dinged. I turned instinctively. [M]Mary[-M] walked in. She wasn't rushing, but she moved with a strange, distracted urgency. She looked... lost.
(Muttering to herself) Bread... milk... what else was it...
I was less than three feet away from her. I expected her to spot me, to smile, to ask why I wasn't in class.
But she didn't even look at me.
She walked right past me, her eyes fixed on the shelves but not really seeing them. She was completely deep in thought, biting her lip nervously.
Right... dinner. Just make dinner. Act normal.
She approached the counter. She was fumbling with her purse, looking for her wallet, dropping a few coins on the floor in her clumsiness.
[M]Mary[-M]? You okay? You seem a million miles away.
(Startled) Oh! Natalie. I... yes. I'm fine. Just... a lot on my mind today. A bit scattered, I suppose.
She gave a weak, polite smile that didn't reach her eyes. She put a twenty on the counter, her movements jerky and uncoordinated.
...Right. That'll be twelve bucks.
Here. Keep the change, dear. I really must be going.
(To herself) Keys... where are the keys... ah, here.
She hurried out the door, the bell jingling behind her. She looked like someone trying very hard to hold it together and failing slightly.
...Weird. She usually asks about my classes.
She walked right past you. Didn't even say hi?
I... guess she didn't see me. She seemed really out of it.
"Out of it"? Dude, look at her.
I've seen that look. That's not just "out of it." She looks like she's either running from a ghost... or running late to get railed.
That's... a weird thing to say.
Is it? Look at the flush on her chest. The fidgeting. The "I need to go right now" panic.
(Running from a ghost... to get railed.)
(She's right. And we both know who the ghost is. And who's waiting to do the railing.)

s2_priscilla_route_063.text: After the day's final lecture, as the halls emptied, my ears caught the faint, tantalizing rush of water echoing softly nearby.
Glancing around carefully, it suddenly clicked-it was coming from the women's changing rooms. The gentle hiss of someone in the showers drew me in like a moth to a flame.
(There's no fucking way we're passing up a chance to peek at whatever hot little morsel is soaking herself in there…)
(But… what if someone catches us?!)
(Are you fucking kidding me right now? After everything we've pulled lately, spying in the women's showers is suddenly off-limits? Grow some balls, man!)
(It's not that… I just… Well, it's risky…)
(Nobody's gonna see shit. These undergrads are practically sprinting home to jerk off and stuff their dumb faces. Trust me, we're golden.)
(Fuck… Okay, just a quick look, alright?)
(Now we're talking! Let's sneak into the showers and-)
And just what do you think you're doing hanging around here, [MC]Peter[-MC]?
(Oh shit.)
[CHOICE]
I go where I want, Professor. It's a free campus.
Not near the women's locker room, you don't. Why are you even going there? Turn around and walk away before I make this a disciplinary issue. Let's try this conversation again.
I was looking for a lost item. I thought maybe I dropped it near here.
Right in front of the women's showers? That's highly unlikely, and frankly, inappropriate. There is no reason for you to be here. Go look somewhere else, [MC]Peter[-MC]. Try again.
I was actually looking for you, Professor.
Looking for me? Down this hallway? I find that hard to believe. What could you possibly need right now?
[CHOICE]
Well, you always smell so nice after a shower, Sara. I couldn't resist.
Excuse me? That is completely inappropriate for the middle of a university hallway. Stop acting like a creep. Why are you even hovering around here? Leave now.
I heard a weird noise coming from inside and got worried.
If there's a noise, campus security handles it, not wandering students. You have no business investigating the women's changing rooms. Get going.
I wanted to ask about my grade on the recent project. I've been really anxious about it.
Your grade? [MC]Peter[-MC], we can discuss academic matters during my designated office hours, not while loitering outside the changing rooms.
Now, please run along. I'm going to stand right here for a moment to make sure you actually leave.
(Damn it, she's standing her ground. I need to get her to leave the area entirely if I want to get inside.)
[CHOICE]
Can't we just discuss it right here? It will only take a minute.
I said no. This is neither the time nor the place, and there is no reason for you to stay in this corridor. Stop stalling and head home, [MC]Peter[-MC].
Move aside, Sara. I'm going in anyway.
Take one more step toward that door, and I will personally march you to the Dean's office. Why are you so obsessed with this? You are not going in there. Leave now.
Actually, I think Dean Walter was looking for you earlier. He was pacing near the main office and seemed really upset about something.
Sara's neutral, authoritative expression immediately faltered. A flash of genuine anxiety crossed her face as she remembered her recent, tense encounters with the Dean.
Walter? He was looking for me? Upset?
Yeah, he was muttering something about "liabilities" and "faculty issues." I figured you'd want to know.
(Under her breath) That bastard... he never stops.
She quickly smoothed down her skirt, completely forgetting about me and the shower door.
Fine. Thank you for the information, [MC]Peter[-MC]. I need to go deal with this immediately. Don't cause any trouble while I'm gone.
Without another word, Sara practically sprinted down the opposite end of the corridor, her heels clicking rapidly against the tiles.
(Hahaha! Hook, line, and sinker.)
(Now the coast is completely clear. Let's get inside and see what kind of wet prize is waiting for us.)
I smirked, stepping up to the now unguarded door of the women's changing rooms, my heart pounding with anticipation.

s2_basement_wine_first.text: (A massive mahogany cabinet filled with bottles that are probably older than I am. The glass is dusty, but the labels look pristine.)
(Château Margaux. Pétrus. Romanee-Conti. There’s enough money in this cabinet to buy my entire neighborhood.)
(Liquid courage. Or liquid oblivion. Look at the empty spaces on the shelf. She comes down here a lot, doesn’t she?)
Her voice cuts through the air, sharp and impatient.
Stop staring at the bottles, [MC]Peter[-MC]. Those vintages are wasted on a palate like yours.

s2_priscilla_route_015_1.text: The moment we stepped into the café, Priscilla launched into her usual tirade, picking apart everything I did. It felt endless and utterly unbearable.
Honestly, [MC]Peter[-MC], how have you survived this long thinking Caesar is just a salad? How are you even functional?
Keep it up, princess, and I'll show you how to toss a salad.
You don't toss salads, you idiot! God, you're pathetic. You wouldn’t last a single day with real responsibilities.
If daddy had to put up with you, he'd disown you faster than he'd fire a lazy servant.
(God, poor Harry. Living with this spoiled brat must be hell.)
(Actually, she's kind of entertaining. I enjoy her bitchy attitude.)
(Seriously? Even you can't enjoy her constant whining.)
(Come on, beneath that bitchy exterior lies an obedient little rich girl, desperate to be ordered around.)
(I thought you liked women who take control.)
(Only occasionally. Honestly, I don't buy her tough act. I bet she'd melt with the right commands whispered in her ear.)
Hey, dumbass! Are you even listening?
Hm? Yeah, sure, absolutely.
Oh really? Then what was I just saying?
Probably something about your daddy, horse racing, and those filthy peasants you always complain about.
You're absolutely hopeless! If you'd been paying attention, you'd know I emailed you some of the project work I've already done. Idiot.
Wait, you actually did some of the project?
Of course I did! Contrary to your pathetic assumptions, I'm not stupid.
Forget it. I'm going to the restroom. Try not to screw anything else up while I'm gone.
(Finally, some peace.)
(You know what's even better than peace?)
(What now?)
(The fact that I managed to swipe this from her bag without her noticing.)
(What the hell? How did you pull that off?)
(Easy. She's just as oblivious as you are when she's ranting.)
(But why? What are you planning?)
(Relax, I have an idea. A very profitable idea.)
(Oh god, I don't like where this is headed...)
(Bingo. Here's daddy Harry’s mobile number.)
(Shouldn't you write it down?)
(Not necessary. I'm your subconscious, remember? I don’t forget anything worth remembering.)
(Plus, leaving evidence is never wise.)
(So, you're going to blackmail Harry, aren’t you?)
(No, [MC]Peter[-MC], WE'RE going to blackmail him.)
(What's your endgame? Seriously, what's driving you?)
(Call it an experiment. I want to confirm my suspicions about the kind of man Harry truly is.)
(Experiment, my ass. You just want to manipulate the situation to your advantage.)
(Come on, lighten up. The only thing you should be taking seriously is a hard cock, and we're working on that.)
Priscilla returned from the restroom, looking refreshed and just as arrogant as before.
Alright, we're leaving. I'll pay. I'm not going to let you embarrass me by fumbling with loose change at the counter.
She turned and walked to the counter to pay, leaving her handbag unzipped on our table for a moment as she pulled out her wallet.
(Now. While the queen is distracted by her gold. Perfect.)
With a movement so quick and smooth it barely registered, I slipped her phone from my pocket back into the open handbag on the table. She wouldn't even know it had been gone.
(See? A perfect crime. She'll never even know her little world was in our hands.)
Priscilla returned, tucking her wallet away with a dismissive air.
There. My social obligation to not be seen dining alone is fulfilled. You're dismissed. I have actual shopping to do.
Without another glance, she turned and walked off towards the more expensive boutiques.
(Works for me. We got what we came for.)
(I watched her go, a small smile on my face. Her insults didn't sting anymore. They were just noise.)
Turning in the opposite direction, I headed for the exit. The real game had just begun.

s2_sara_route_053.text: I was walking down the hallway when I saw Becca ahead of me. She was heading straight for the administrative wing.
She turned the corner, making a beeline for Sara's office door.
(She's just dropping by to see Sara. No big deal.)
(Oh, you think so? Grab some popcorn. This is going to be the season finale.)
I stopped. There was something in Red's voice—a dark, sadistic anticipation—that made my blood run cold.
(What did you do?)
(Me? Nothing much. Just left a little housewarming gift during our last visit.)
(Red. What did you do?)
(Remember when you "zoned out" for a second while she was fixing her hair? I slipped your boxers into her purse.)
(The expensive one. The one sitting wide open on her desk right now.)
My heart stopped.
(You... you put my dirty underwear in her bag?!)
(Right on top. If Becca so much as glances inside, she's going to see your initials staring right back at her.)
I looked down the hall. Becca was ten feet from the door. Five feet.
(Oh my god. She's going to see them.)
Panic exploded in my chest. I lunged forward, opening my mouth to scream.
BECC—!
(Shhh. Don't spoil the surprise. Let's watch the fireworks.)
(Let me go! You're going to destroy everything!)
(Exactly. Chaos is a ladder, Peter. Watch her fall.)
I couldn't speak. I couldn't run. Becca reached for the handle.
With a desperate surge of will, I forced my fingers to move. Not to run, but to type.
HIDE YOUR PURSE! NOW!
MY BOXERS ARE INSIDE! BECCA IS AT THE DOOR!
I hit send just as Becca knocked and opened the door in one motion.
(Buzzkill.)
I ducked behind the corner, peering through the small window.
I saw Sara looking at her phone. Her eyes bulged. She looked at the open designer bag on her desk—and the grey fabric clearly visible inside.
Then she looked up and saw Becca walking in.
Hey, Sara! Do you have a sec?
Sara moved faster than I’d ever seen a human move. She threw a stack of grading papers over the open bag, burying it just as the door opened fully.
Becca!!
Whoa! Jesus, you scared me! I just wanted to borrow a pen!
Becca stepped closer, walking around the side of the desk to get to where the bag was sitting under the pile.
I think I saw a spare one in your bag yest—
NO!
Stop! Don't come any closer!
...What? Why? It's just a pen, Sara.
Confidential! Everything on this desk is highly confidential! University policy! No students allowed behind the desk! Not even you!
Okay... you're acting insane. Is everything alright?
Yes! Fine! Just... protocol! Strict protocol!
I actually need to lock up. Right now. Secret meeting. Can we talk later?
Uh, sure... I'll just go find [MC]Peter[-MC] then...
Yes! Find him! Go! Bye!
Sara practically pushed Becca out of the office, slamming the door shut the second she was in the hallway.
Through the window, I saw her lean back against the door, sliding down to the floor, her hand over her heart. She looked like she was about to have a heart attack.
(Look at that adrenaline. She's never felt more alive.)
(She's going to kill us.)
My phone buzzed.
You are a monster.
I just saved your life. You're welcome.
But next time... keep a closer eye on your panties. And mine.
(Next time, I'll make sure she wears them.)

s2_gerda_route_061_e_darnell.text: The afternoon sun beats down on the university sports ground.
I’m just walking by, trying to clear my head, when I spot them through the chain-link fence.
She’s in the push-up position on the red rubberized track, her face strained, sweat dripping from her nose.
He’s standing over her, legs spread, like a king surveying his subject.
(Look at how tight her workout gear is... Her gray sports bra is practically soaked, barely containing her heavy breaths.)
(And Darnell... he's just standing there, enjoying the view of her cleavage every time she goes down.)
Down. Up. Faster, girl! You think the competition is gonna wait for you to catch your breath?
My girl’s gotta be number one.
(My girl. The words twist in my gut like a knife. He says it so easily. Like he owns her.)
He places his foot on her lower back, his sneaker pressing right where her spine meets the curve of her ass.
He's applying just enough pressure to make the exercise agonizingly harder.
It’s not encouragement. It’s a fucking power play.
A way to feel her body flex and strain right beneath his shoe.
I’m… trying. The heat is…
Darnell's stern expression suddenly shifts into a sickeningly smug, lecherous grin.
He knows exactly what he's doing to her, and he loves it.
The heat is an excuse. Excuses are for losers.
You’re not a loser, are you, [T]Tiffany[-T]?
She grits her teeth, her voice tight with suppressed anger and exhaustion.
Her arms are trembling, making her firm, round ass jiggle slightly with the effort.
No. I’m not a loser.
She pushes through another rep, her muscles burning, before finally collapsing onto her stomach on the hot track, panting heavily.
Good. Now on your feet. I wanna see sprints.
As she struggles up to her knees, he reaches out and gives her sweat-slicked ass a hard, possessive smack.
*SMACK!*
It's not playful. It’s a brand. A loud, echoing mark of ownership for anyone watching.
The sound makes my own hands curl into tight fists against the chain-link fence.
(And what are you going to do about it, hero? Stand here behind the fence and clench your fists like a little bitch? He owns her.)
(He’s marking his territory, and you’re just a stray dog watching through the wire.)
(I want to tear him apart. I want to smash his smug face into the track. But I can’t. Not yet.)
(Of course you can’t. He’s an alpha. Look at how he treats that tight, athletic body.)
(He uses it however he pleases.)
(But you… you own someone, too. Someone bigger.)
(Softer. Someone who doesn’t fight back.)
(Someone who would beg to thank you for putting your foot on her back.)
(My breathing quickens. The image of Darnell’s boot pinning [T]Tiffany[-T] down morphs in my mind… into the image of my own hand, my cock, my entire being dominating someone else.)
(Someone whose holes are already wet for me.)
(Don’t waste this fire on jealousy. Anger and humiliation? That's the best fucking aphrodisiac there is. Let’s channel it.)
(Let’s go find someone who will appreciate all this wonderful, violent energy.)
(Someone who’s probably spreading her legs dreaming about you right now.)
I stand up straight, my muscles coiled tight with a dark, furious, lustful resolve.
The sight of [T]Tiffany[-T] wiping her face, her beautiful spirit being ground down under his thumb… it’s too much to just watch.
I turn away from the chain-link fence, my hand already reaching for my phone, a massive bulge straining against my zipper.
(He’s right. Fuck this. Fuck Darnell. I’m going to find my own release. My own subject.)

s2_gerda_backyard_bush.text: (These hydrangea bushes are really overgrown. I better trim them properly if I want to keep this "gardener" cover story believable.)

(Overgrown? Pffft. They're perfect for hiding behind while that bitch Priscilla changes by the window... Or better yet, we can 'accidentally' leave some shears near the pool and hope that arrogant hag Gerda trips on them.)

Hurry up and fetch your tools! The weeds are practically growing as we speak.

s2_sara_route_012.text: The lecture hall was nearly empty. Down at the podium, Sara was struggling with her briefcase.
(Muttering) Damn it... fit, you stupid thing...
A folder slipped from her hands, spilling papers across the floor.
No, no, no!
Need a hand with that?
She jumped, spinning around. She hadn't heard me walking down the steps.
[MC]Peter[-MC]! I thought everyone had left.
I was just packing up. Here, let me help.
I knelt down to gather the papers. Her hand shot out, snatching a sheet away before I could touch it.
I can manage! I don't need your help.
You're shaking, Professor.
I am not shaking. It's... too much coffee. I've had a long day. Now, please, step back.
It looks like more than just coffee. You've been dropping things all lecture.
Is there a point to this observation? Or are you just here to critique my motor skills?
I'm just worried. You seem really on edge lately.
"On edge"?
Yeah. Tense. Jumpier than usual.
My mood is not up for discussion, [MC]Peter[-MC]. If you have a question about the coursework, ask it. Otherwise, leave.
I saw you earlier today. Outside. You looked terrified.
Excuse me?
When you were talking to Darnell. You looked like you were afraid of him.
She let out a sharp, incredulous laugh, but it sounded brittle.
Afraid? Of a student? That is ridiculous.
Was it? You were backing away from him.
I was ending a conversation with a difficult student. Darnell can be... persistent. That is all.
It looked like he was threatening you. Or maybe holding something over you?
That is enough!
You are crossing a line. My private conversations are none of your business.
I'm just trying to help. If he's bothering you—
I handle my own problems! I don't need a white knight, especially not one who should be focusing on his failing grades!
My grades are fine.
Then I'll make sure they aren't! Keep prying into my life, and you'll find yourself failing this course faster than you can blink. Do I make myself clear?
...Crystal clear.
Good. Now get out.
Sure. Just... take it easy, Professor. You really don't look well.
I said out!
I turned and walked up the stairs.
I didn't look back, but I heard the sound of her finally collapsing into her chair, the leather creaking under her weight.
(She's cracking. And she knows we saw right through her.)

s2_gerda_route_067_1_b_panic.text: I spent the evening in a state of low-grade panic. Every car that passed by outside made me jump.
[M]Mary[-M] was humming in the kitchen, completely oblivious to the impending disaster. She wiped her hands on a towel and glanced out the window.
Oh, my goodness. [MC]Peter[-MC], dear, come look at this car. I've never seen anything so fancy in our neighborhood.
I walked to the window and saw the long, black Tercedes parked at our curb. It looked like a hearse for rich people.
Gerda emerged. Even from here, I could see the sharp, predatory focus in her movements.
She surveyed our small lawn not with disgust, but with the cold calculation of a general inspecting a battlefield.
Wait a minute... isn't that... Mrs. Sterling? Priscilla's mother?
What on earth is she doing here again? Did something happen at the university?
(Think, think, think! stick to the story.)
U-uh, no! Nothing's wrong, [M]Mary[-M]. She's... she's here to see me.
She turned to me, her face a mask of confusion.
It's... the scholarship thing! The project we talked about. She's a patron of the university, you know. Just... checking in on my progress.
The doorbell rang, sharp and imperious. It sounded less like a request for entry and more like a command.
[M]Mary[-M] looked from me to the door, her brow furrowed with skepticism, but she smoothed her apron.
Well... alright, dear. Don't keep her waiting.

s2_opening_029.text: I looked at the small door tucked under the stairs.
It was boarded up cross-wise with three thick wooden planks. It had been like that for years.
"Safety hazard." That was always the official excuse. "Unstable foundation."
(Move along. Nothing to see here. Just wood and dust.)
Wait.
I stepped closer, narrowing my eyes. The wood was old and gray... but something caught the light.
One of the nails on the bottom plank was shiny. Silver.
(That nail is new. The others are rusted shut. This one... looks fresh.)
I looked down at the floorboards near the doorframe.
Faint, dried muddy footprints leading FROM the basement door TO the center of the room. They are barely visible against the wood grain, fading out near the rug.
(Mud? Inside? It hasn't rained in days.)
(And the tracks... they're coming out of the basement.)
Red... did you...?
(I said move along. Focus on the mission.)
You've been down there. While I was asleep. You unsealed it.
(There are rats down there. Big ones. Mutants. I was securing the perimeter. Protecting the house. You're welcome.)
(Stop looking at the floor. Look at the room. This is boring exposition.)
(He’s deflecting. He’s definitely hiding something down there.)
I wanted to pry deeper, maybe even pull at the board, but the basement was a mystery for another time. I had a feeling whatever was down there wasn't going to stay buried for long.
I stepped back, leaving the secrets in the dark for now.

s2_sara_route_001.text: I was walking through the old faculty wing hallway. It was quiet this time of day, usually empty.
I heard voices up ahead, just around the corner. One was definitely Sara's.
The other was a man's voice, deep, older, and sharp.
...and I trust you won't be making the same... administrative errors... as your predecessor, Sara. The board was very disappointed last time.
I leaned against the wall, peering just enough to see the hallway. I could see Sara standing there, but the man she was talking to was hidden around the corner, out of sight.
I couldn't see his face, but I could hear the cold authority in his tone. He wasn't speaking to her like a colleague. He sounded like a disappointed boss.
Sara’s usually rigid posture was gone. She stood in the middle of the hall, shoulders slightly hunched, head bowed.
No, Professor Albright. I assure you, everything is in order. It won't happen again.
See that it doesn't. Your position here is a privilege, not a right. Don't forget who granted it to you.
There was a heavy pause. I held my breath, afraid to make a sound on the tile floor.
I heard heavy footsteps walking away in the opposite direction, the sound fading down the corridor.
Sara stood there for a long moment, completely still, staring at the floor.
Then she slowly straightened up, smoothing her skirt, trying to pull herself back together. But for a second, she looked exhausted.
(What was that about? "The board"? "What happened last time"?)
(Well, look at that. The Ice Queen takes orders just like everyone else. She sounded scared.)
(That wasn't just respect, pal. That was fear. And fear is something we can use.)

s2_clara_route_007.text: Clara, as usual, was standing there, looking slightly worn out by life, with that eternal exhaustion in her eyes. Almost pitiful to look at.
But the second she spotted me, her eyes went wide, a flash of fear and curiosity flickering through them.
(Or maybe I just imagined it-did I see some twisted fucking hope in there too?)
Can I help you with something, sir?
Here’s your cash, sweetheart. Every last fucking cent.
You… you actually did it? I… I can’t believe my fucking eyes!
Yeah, trust me, I won’t be forgetting that shit anytime soon.
Clara suddenly burst into sobs and bolted toward the bathroom.
(Oh, for fuck’s sake, here we go again…)

s2_opening_035.text: [M]Mary[-M] stepped off the stairs and into the living room.
She was back in her usual house clothes and an apron. Her face was bright red, her eyes fixed firmly on the floorboards to avoid looking at me.
I want to apologize. I was... flustered. I didn't mean to-
No, let me finish! I am the adult here! I need to set an example!
She lifted her head, squaring her shoulders, trying to regain her dignity. She looked like she was about to give a speech.
We are going to pretend that-
Her gaze traveled past me. Past [T]Tiffany[-T]. And landed directly on the center window.
Is that... is that a tumor?

s2_clara_route_006.text: As I approached the campus corridor, I could hear it again, the sound of quiet, desperate sobbing. I saw Clara ahead, trying to mop the floor, but her movements were weak, broken. She kept her head down, as if the weight of the world was crushing her.
My presence made her look up. She tried to hastily wipe her tears, tried to fumble out some words, her face a swollen, red mess.
H-hello *sniff* sir, h-h-how are.., you?
(The pain in her eyes was raw. This was more than just a bad day. This was a complete breakdown.)
Why are you crying, Clara?
She just shook her head, another wave of tears streaming down her face. She leaned heavily on the mop, as if it was the only thing holding her up.
I-I..can’t… It’s just… everything, sir. I’m such a failure… a terrible mother…
(A wave of pity and crushing awkwardness washed over me. What was I supposed to do? Pat her on the back? Tell her 'there, there'? I was so fucking useless in moments like these.)
Oh…okay.

Clara’s face fell even further at my pathetic, mumbled response. Her eyes, which had held a tiny flicker of hope, went dull with despair. She was hoping for… something. Anything. And I had failed her.
(Of course you failed her, you idiot. You don't know how to handle a real woman's pain. Let me take over. I do.)
(No! You’ll just make it worse! You’ll be cruel!)
(Just for once, trust me! Don’t you wanna help the damsel in distress and all that bullshit? I know exactly what she needs to hear.)

I didn't wait for permission. I walked out of the room, following the sound of running footsteps echoing down the long university corridor.
(The hunt is on. And both of our pets need to be disciplined.)

s2_ending_002.text: I walked into the kitchen to grab a glass of water. [T]Tiffany[-T] was leaning against the counter, fanning herself aggressively with a magazine.
She was wearing her workout gear, her skin glistening with a fresh layer of sweat. She looked miserable and incredibly annoyed.
Don't even look at me, Ogre. I am one degree away from spontaneous combustion.
It's not outside, it's my damn room! The AC vent is just blowing warm, dusty air. It's literally a greenhouse in there.
(Working exactly as planned. Look at the sweat pooling on her collarbone. She's roasting.)
Of course I told [M]Mary[-M]. She said she's not calling emergency maintenance at night because they charge double. She told me to "open a window and build character."
She wiped her forehead with the back of her hand, her chest heaving with an annoyed sigh.
(I took a slow sip of my water, keeping my face completely neutral.)
Weird, though. My room is practically a freezer. I'm actually thinking about putting on a sweater. I don't even need my desk fan tonight.
[T]Tiffany[-T] paused her fanning. She narrowed her eyes at me, a mix of pure envy and suspicion.
You have a desk fan? The big metal one?
Yeah. Just sitting there gathering dust. Anyway, good luck building character.
(Drop the mic and walk away. Leave the bait dangling right in front of her face.)
I turned and walked out of the kitchen. I could feel her eyes burning a hole in my back.
(She took the bait. She's too stubborn to ask for it now, but wait until midnight. The heat will break her pride.)

BarInside_01.text: Morning. Don't ask for a Mojito. I'm out of mint.
Info costs a drink. And since I'm not serving, you're out of luck.
Come on. Everyone talks to the bartender.
That's the problem. They talk. I listen. And then I forget. It's the only way to stay sane in this town.
If I remembered half the things Alan told me, I'd have to shoot myself.

s2_dress_shop_checkout_counter.text: (Empty again. Seriously, does anyone in this mall actually work the cash register? It's like a ghost town behind every counter in this town.)

(Oh, they're 'working' alright. Just not the register. I bet the cashier is in the stockroom right now getting her 'inventory' rearranged by some manager. Want me to hop over the counter and offer some hands-on customer support?)
(Gross. No. Can we just wait for an employee like normal people? I'm not getting arrested for jumping a counter just because you have a kink for retail workers.)
(Suit yourself, square. But if she comes out panting with her nametag on backward, I'm calling dibs.)

s2_gerda_route_009_.text: I sank deeper into the worn-out couch, my muscles still aching miserably from all that damned gardening at Gerda’s place.
Clicking through the TV channels aimlessly, I desperately hoped my favorite show might magically appear and distract me from my current misery.
(Really, [MC]Peter[-MC]? All these hot chicks roaming around town, and you’re wasting your time sitting here hoping some stupid show pops up to save your pathetic day?)
(Just as I was about to snap back at Red’s annoying commentary, the door flew open with a loud bang.)
Gerda stood there, her pristine white dress practically glowing as she scanned my shitty little place with open disgust.
[M]Mary[-M] immediately scurried over, flashing an awkward smile.
Oh, Mrs. Sterling! You're here already! Please, come in... I wasn't expecting you so soon, the house is a bit of a mess...
Oh, God, [M]Mary[-M]. Now I finally see just how cheaply you live. This dump screams desperation and poverty. Truly charming.
Yeah, Mrs. Gerda, we’re just poor and miserable over here. But at least we don’t drown our loneliness in gallons of morning wine.
Adorable, sweetheart. You’ve got such a… unique way with words. Probably from a lack of proper upbringing.
Well, hello, [MC]Peter[-MC]. I thought I’d drop by and see what kind of shithole our favorite gardener calls home. Now I get why you always look so damn miserable.
Glad you finally see how low-maintenance I am.
And you sleep on this? Jesus, poor young guy, no wonder you’re always so fucking grumpy. You need a decent mattress… or at least a woman worth a damn to share it with.
Actually, we’re doing just fine here without your damn advice.
Sure, honey. Perfect setup for a girl whose career’s heading straight to waitressing at some greasy spoon.
Gerda turned her attention back to me, smirking as she sized up my place and lingered on me a bit too long.
You know, [MC]Peter[-MC], I’m honestly shocked a pathetic little guy like you can pull off that confident act sometimes. Maybe there’s something to you…
…buried real deep, I bet. Maybe one day I’ll figure out your little secret.
Sweetie, you should air this place out. It’s getting hot in here… or is that just me?
Yes, of course… I’ll open the windows…
I’ll let myself out, [MC]Peter[-MC]. This was fun, but I think your “potential” might shine better somewhere else.
(Red, what the fuck was that?)
(That, my friend, was the “Purebred Bitch of the Year” award in action. And I think we’ve got her hooked.)
(Thanks for the visit, Gerda. Next time I’ll hide my dignity better so it doesn’t scare you off again.)
(Don’t worry, she’ll figure out soon enough we’ve got nothing to hide… literally.)
I sighed, shook my head, and sank back into the couch.
(Already plotting how to play this next.)

s2_basement_portrait_repeat.text: (The portrait sits in the gloom. The father's painted eyes seem to follow me.)
(That scratch on his cheek... it’s the only flaw in the perfection. A tiny, violent secret.)
(So, our queen has a history of rebellion. A very... precise history. This just keeps getting more and more interesting.)

You can't train if you hidin' the body, Mary. I need to see the mechanics. I need to see what's jiggling when you move.
I don't feel comfortable wearing tight clothes here, Darnell. Not right now. I'm not... twenty anymore.
(Chuckles) Yeah, I can see that. But baggy clothes don't fix the problem. They just cover it up. You hidin' from yourself, not me.
Can we just start? Please? Before I change my mind.
We are startin'. Step one: reality check.
He pointed chin toward the corner.
Hit the scale. Let's see the damage.
I... I'd rather not today. I know I've gained a little since last time, but—
A little? Miss M, come on. Stop lying to yourself. You wanna get fit, or you wanna play pretend like you usually do?
I want to get fit. Truly. But I don't need to do this right here...
Nobody cares but me and you. Now go on. Unless you scared of a number?
[M]Mary[-M] bit her lip.
I am not scared. Fine.
She walked over to the scale, trying to maintain some dignity under his watchful eye. She stepped onto the platform.
The machine beeped. The numbers settled. [M]Mary[-M] stared at the digital display, her shoulders slumping instantly. The defiance drained out of her. It was worse than she thought.
Oh... that's... that's more than last month.
Damn. That number real?
I... I've been stress-eating lately. Cooking a lot for [MC]Peter[-MC]... tasting everything...
Yeah, I can tell. That ain't just stress, Mary. That's neglect. You stopped tryin'.
Stand up straight. You slouchin' cause you embarrassed?
I'm not slouching.
Shoulders back. Chest out. Stop tryin' to shrink. You a big woman, own it.
Reluctantly, she straightened her spine, obeying the command almost instinctively.
There it is. Heavy, huh? Gravity ain't your friend right now.
Darnell, please... you're being rude.
I'm bein' honest. Somebody has to be. [MC]Peter[-MC] probably too nice to tell you you gettin' sloppy, right? He just eats your food and smiles.
(Her voice tight) Leave him out of this.
I'm just sayin'. He sees it too. He sees you wobblin' around the kitchen in that bathrobe. Probably feels bad for you.
[M]Mary[-M]'s face flushed a deep red. Shame burned in her eyes. The idea of me pitying her clearly hurt more than his mockery.
He reached out and poked her side, right above the hip, through the loose gray shirt. Not hard, just a prod to emphasize his point. His finger sank deep into the softness.
Squishy.
Soft. Like dough. No muscle tone at all under here, is there?
Don't... don't touch me there. Please.
Why? It's just fat, Mary. We gotta know what we workin' with.
He gave her waist a little shake, watching the way her body moved under the fabric.
See that jiggle? That's what happens when you skip gym days. You let yourself go, Mary. You turned into a pillow.
I'm here, Darnell. I did exactly what you said on the phone.
Darnell stepped back, looking bored. He wiped his hands on his shirt as if he'd touched something greasy.
Nah. Not today.
What? What do you mean?
Look at you. You're shakin'. You're soft. You ain't ready for the weights today. You'll just hurt yourself and waste my time.
You ain't ready for the gym floor, Mary. People gonna laugh if they see you jiggling around like this. I can't be seen trainin' a pillow.
(Stunned) So... that's it? You're sending me away? After I did everything you asked?
I'm sendin' you to the locker room. Training's over for today.
Go get changed. Put your regular clothes back on.
But... we haven't discussed anything. The plan... the schedule... what do I do next?
We'll discuss the... specific terms... later.
Later? When is later?
(Shrugging) Whenever I decide you're ready to listen. Now go. Before I change my mind and make you do burpees right here in front of everyone.
[M]Mary[-M] bit her lip, looking torn between humiliation and relief.
Fine... I'll go.
(He actually let her go. He just humiliated her and sent her packing.)
(Maybe he really is just disgusted by how she looks?)
I looked back at Darnell. He watched her disappear into the hallway. He didn't move to follow her immediately.
He just stood there, checking his phone, looking completely unbothered.
(You really buy that? "We'll discuss it later"?)
(Don't be naive. He didn't send her away to let her go home. He sent her away to get her isolated.)
(But he's just standing there...)
(He's giving her a head start. He knows she's going to be alone in that locker room, half-naked and vulnerable, waiting to get changed.)
(He's not done with her. He's just moving the meeting to somewhere private. We need to follow her. Now.)

s2_ntr_route_025.text: Dude, what is UP with her?
Don't play dumb. She's been acting like a cornered rabbit for days.
I asked her where the laundry detergent was this morning, and she literally jumped.
She's probably just stressed. You know she worries about everything around the house.
Yeah, but this is a different kind of stressed. I've got a theory.
I'm calling it right now. She’s either going through early menopause, or... she’s got a secret boy toy at that gym and she’s just severely under-fucked.
A boy toy? [T]Tiffany[-T], come on. That's [M]Mary[-M] we're talking about. She wouldn't do that.
Oh, please. You're so naive, [MC]Peter[-MC]. Women have needs too, you know. Have you seen her coming back from the gym lately?
She is completely flushed, her clothes are a mess, and she can barely walk up the stairs! She winces every time she sits down. That's not just "cardio."
You're reading way too much into this.
I'm just calling it like I see it! I bet some huge, sweaty meathead trainer is absolutely wrecking her every afternoon, and she's too embarrassed to admit it to us.
(She has no idea how close she is to the actual truth. It makes me sick.)
(Heh. "Boy toy" is a cute way to put it. "New owner" is much more accurate. And he's definitely wrecking her, just not with the romantic movie-montage vibe this clueless brat thinks.)
You have a wild imagination, Tiff. I seriously doubt she's hooking up with anyone.
Whatever. Keep living in your innocent little bubble. But mark my words, that pent-up, jumpy energy she's giving off?
It's totally gross to think about, but the woman clearly needs to get laid.

s2_priscilla_route_027.text: (The morning air feels different today. Like victory.)
(Don’t get a boner for yourself just yet, champ. One successful movie date doesn’t make you James Bond. But… I’ll admit, you were slightly less pathetic than usual.)
(This is my chance. Just be cool. Say something cool.)
(Yeah, go on. Walk over there. Show her who’s the boss now.)
Hey, Priscilla. Good morning.
Well, well. Look who it is, Pris. Isn't that your little... friend from last night?
Shut up, Stacy. Don't invent things. It makes you look desperate.
I’m just saying. You two looked *so* cozy leaving the theater.
Wait, for real? You hanging out with the help now, Princess?
I said shut up! I was doing charity work.
Priscilla? I thought we... you know...
You thought what? That because I let you carry my trash, we're friends?
Aww, he looks heartbroken. Come on, Pris, introduce us to your boyfriend properly.
He is *not* my boyfriend, you bleached-blonde idiot!
Do I know you? No. You’re a gardener. A gnat.
But... you said...
I said get out of my sight. You’re embarrassing yourself.
I think he’s cute, in a pathetic sort of way. Maybe he can fetch my coffee next? Since you're done with him?
Take him. He smells like poverty and desperation. He’ll fit right in with your aesthetic, Stacy.
Priscilla, I didn't mean to-
Didn't mean to what? Exist? Because you're failing at that, too.
Now move. You're blocking the view, and you're giving Stacy ammunition. I don't associate with losers.
You heard the lady. Scram, trash punk.
(And... down goes the hero. She sacrificed you to win a point against Stacy. Brutal.)
Call me if you want a real job, [MC]Peter[-MC]!
Shut UP, Stacy!
(I’m still just a fucking loser.)

s2_sara_route_016_pot.text: I knelt down beside the large ceramic pot. It held a decorative fern.
This screams "hidden key." Oldest trick in the book.
Okay, how do I look for it?
[CHOICE FRAME]
I tilted the heavy pot. Nothing but wet concrete and bugs.
Great job, Hercules. Try again.
I shook the fern. Leaves rustled loudly.
Quiet! You want to wake up the whole neighborhood?
I stuck my hand into the damp soil. Cold and slimy.
I raked the top layer. Just moss and dirt.
It's buried, genius. Go deeper.
[CHOICE FRAME]
Maybe it's round the back?
I checked the other side. Still nothing.
You're just petting the dirt now. Dig down!
Fine. I shoved my hand deeper into the mud.
Wait... I feel something hard!
My heart skipped a beat. It was flat and metallic.
Got it!
I yanked it out triumphantly, scattering dirt everywhere.
I opened my hand. It wasn't a key. It was an old, rusty bottle cap.
...Seriously? A bottle cap?
Red burst into laughter.
Congratulations. You found trash.
Darnell isn't hiding his key in a bottle cap. Keep digging, trash-picker.
[CHOICE FRAME]
This is gross. My hand is freezing.
We are NOT leaving empty-handed. Get back in there!
I gritted my teeth and plunged my hand all the way to the bottom of the pot.
(Come on... come on...)
My fingers scraped against the ceramic bottom... and hooked onto a small metal ring.
Okay. This is definitely it.
I pulled it out slowly.
Finally.
I rubbed the key against the rough fabric of my jeans, clearing away the thick layer of dirt until the silver metal gleamed faintly.
See? Persistence pays off. Now wipe that mud on your pants and open the door.

s2_priscilla_route_011_0.text: On a hunch, I walked over to her nightstand. The top was cluttered with expensive creams and chargers. I tried the drawer. It slid open silently.
It was mostly tidy books, a tablet, but something metallic caught my eye, shoved all the way to the very back, half-buried under an old notebook.
(What's that? It doesn't belong with the rest of her stuff.)
Curiosity getting the better of me, I reached in and pulled it out. It felt cold and heavy in my palm.
It was a medal. Not gold, like the ones proudly displayed on the shelves, but dull silver. I flipped it over to read the engraving.
*"Equestrian Regionals - 2nd Place"*
(Second place? Why is this hidden in the back of her drawer? It's still a good achievement...)
(For normal people? Sure. For Princess Priscilla, the girl who needs everyone to see her as flawless? This isn't an achievement.)
(It's a failure. A dirty little secret of mediocrity.)
I looked from the shining gold trophies on the wall to the dull silver medal in my hand, hidden away in the dark.
(Well, well, well. We didn't come looking for dirt, but we just stumbled onto gold. Or silver, I guess.)
(A hidden mark of shame for a girl who thinks she's perfect. Pocket it, champ. I think we just found the perfect accessory for her next training session.)
Just as I slipped the medal into my pocket, the doorknob turned.
What the hell do you think you're doing?
Her voice was sharp, freezing me in place. I spun around.
Priscilla was standing in the doorway, her arms crossed, looking at me with pure disgust.
(Fuck. I'm dead.)
Did you get lost on the way to the mulch pile, or do you just enjoy spreading your filth around my private space?
I... uh... the door was open. I thought I heard...
She cut me off with a scoff.
Spare me. Get out. Now. Before I have security throw you out with the rest of the trash.
(I kept my hand tight over the pocket where the medal was hidden.)
Sorry, Priscilla. I'm going.
She stepped aside just enough to let me pass, wrinkling her nose as if I smelled bad.
And don't touch anything else with those grubby hands. God, you people have no boundaries.
I hurried past her, heart hammering in my chest. She slammed the door shut behind me.
(Let her act tough. We got exactly what we needed. And she has no idea she just gave us the weapon to break her.)

s2_ntr_route_064.text: Yo! Peter! Wait up, man!
Hey, Taksh. I didn't see you.
Clearly. You were walking like a zombie. You okay, dude? You look kind of... dead.
Thanks. Just... didn't sleep well. A lot on my mind.
Rough night? Or just up late grinding?
Something like that.
Well, wake up, because I have news. Did you see the Famitsu leaks for *Crimson Saga: Rebirth*?
No, I haven't checked anything.
Dude! They completely overhauled the Job System for the western release! It's not turn-based anymore, it's hybrid.
Really? I thought the purists were going to riot over that.
Who cares about the purists? Listen, they buffed the Dark Knight class. It actually scales with HP now.
That sounds... broken. In a good way.
It's insanely broken! We need to pre-order the Deluxe Edition. I need you to run a healer so I can DPS with the new Katana build.
Taksh stopped mid-sentence. His eyes went wide as he looked past my shoulder.
Oh, shit. Don't look now.
What?
The football guys. Darnell's crew. Twelve o'clock.
Two guys in university athletic gear—thick grey hoodies with the team logo—were walking straight toward us. They were massive. Linebackers. I recognized them instantly from the gym.
(Great. Just what I need today.)
Taksh instinctively shifted to the side, pressing himself against the wall to give them room. In a narrow hallway like this, guys like that usually just plow through people like us.
(Muttering) Just keep walking, just keep walking...
I tensed up, expecting them to shoulder-check me or just ignore my existence entirely.
(Don't make eye contact. Just disappear.)
But as they got closer, the lead jock—a guy with a thick neck and a buzzcut—locked eyes with me.
He didn't sneer. He didn't laugh. And he didn't say a word.
Instead, he gave a sharp, almost imperceptible nod. He nudged his friend, and they both stepped aside. They parted, clearing a path for me in the middle of the crowded hall.
They walked past us in total silence, completely ignoring Taksh, but giving me a wide berth. As if I was... someone they knew. Someone they shouldn't touch.
Taksh stood frozen, watching them disappear into the crowd. He slowly turned to look at me, his mouth hanging open.
Dude... what the actual hell was that?
I... I don't know. Maybe they were just in a hurry.
In a hurry? Did you see that? They moved for *you*. That guy nodded at you!
They probably just didn't want to bump into us.
No way. Usually, the football team acts like they own the hallway. That was... respect. Since when are you cool with the O-Line?
You're imagining things, Taksh.
I'm not! That was weirdly respectful. Did you start selling them supplements or something?
(It didn't feel like respect. It felt... weird. Like I was marked.)
(They know. They've seen you at the gym with Darnell. They know you belong to him. That's why they moved. You're the Alpha's pet.)
Just drop it, okay? They're just people. Who cares?
Whoa. Okay, sorry. I just thought it was... impressive.
It's not impressive. Let's just go.
Taksh fell silent, looking hurt by my tone. I felt a pang of guilt, but I couldn't explain the sinking feeling in my gut.
(I tried to shake it off, but Taksh was right. They moved for me. Not because they respect me... but maybe because they know who I'm connected to? God, does everyone know?)

s2_gerda_priscilla_room_exit_closed.text: (I have to get out of here. This room feels too intense, like I'm trespassing in a shrine.)
(I try the handle, but it's not giving... or maybe I'm just too nervous.)
(Nervous? You should be *inspired*. Look at this place, Peter. A perfect ice fortress.)
(You can't just walk away. The secret to her rigid little heart is in one of these drawers, or hidden behind that mountain of medals. Find it.)
(Find it? ...Fine. But only because if she catches me, she'll probably turn me into a lawn ornament. Let's make it quick.)

(You seriously need psychiatric help. Let's just focus on what we came here for and get out.)

(You're disgusting. I am not risking getting permanently banned from the campus library for public indecency. I'll just browse the books normally, thanks.)

s2_tiffany_keyhole_night_stub.text: I pressed my face against the door, squinting through the tiny gap in the lock.
Nothing. It was a complete, pitch-black void.
(The lights are out. I can't see a single thing in there. She must be asleep.)
(Or she's lying awake in the dark. Press your ear to the wood, [MC]Peter[-MC]. Can you hear the bedsprings? A little heavy breathing, maybe?)
(Stop it. It's perfectly quiet. I'm just wasting my time staring into darkness.)
(Your loss. The best things always happen in the dark.)

s2_harry_route_size_panic_repeat.text: (I should probably leave Harry alone in his study for now. He looked like he needed some time to recover.)
(Some time? The old man needs a stiff drink and a pacemaker. We just showed him the weapon of mass destruction that's going to wreck his queen.)
(Give our new "supervisor" a moment to process his new reality. We have "protocols" to prepare for, after all.)

s2_ntr_route_072.text: (God... look at that shape. That bubble butt is perfect.)
I walked up to her. She didn't notice me until I was right there.
Hey. Working hard?
[T]Tiffany[-T] jumped slightly, then looked up. She wiped sweat from her forehead with the back of her hand.
Peter? Did you take a wrong turn? The AC is back inside, you know.
Very funny. I was just... getting some fresh air. Watching the star athlete.
Star athlete? Hardly. I'm just trying to shave a few milliseconds off my 100-meter.
Chantelle is... well, she's a machine this year. If I don't get faster, I'm going to be eating her dust at the finals.
You'll beat her. You always do. You've got better form.
Since when are you an expert on running form? You get winded walking up stairs.
I'm just saying. I believe in you.
Thanks, nerd.
She glanced at my hand. I was holding my phone. In a blur of motion, she snatched it right out of my grip.
But seriously, what are you doing out here? Checking "how to survive direct sunlight"?
Give it back, Tiff. I was reading something.
Nope. Come on, let’s go get smoothies. My treat. You look like a ghost standing out here.
As we were messing around—me reaching for the phone, her laughing and dodging—Darnell approached. He didn't look amused.
Yo. What the fuck is this?
It’s called “messing around.” You should try it, if Chantelle can stand to be near you for more than five seconds.
Chantelle is busy winning. Unlike you.
She botherin’ you, white guy?
What? No, it's Tiffany, we were just—
Stepping between us, getting right in [T]Tiffany[-T]'s personal space.
I said, leave him alone. He’s with me now. You got a problem, you come through me.
Are you fucking kidding me? Get out of my face.
Darnell, stop it. It’s not like that.
Nah, I see how it is. You're weak, Tiff. You can't even beat Chantelle on the track, how you gonna protect him?
Good thing I’m here to keep all you bitches in line.
(Oh my god, he’s making a scene. Everyone is staring… I feel like such a fucking loser.)
Now run along, girl. Go practice. Maybe you won't come in last next time. The men are talkin’.
Unbelievable. You're pathetic.
See? She knows her place. They always run when they realize they can't win.
He didn't say anything else. He just patted my cheek—a sharp, condescending tap—and walked away, leaving me standing there alone in the middle of the track.
(I stood there, watching him walk away. I didn't follow him. I didn't run after Tiffany. I just stood there, paralyzed.)

s2_ntr_route_002.text: (What is she doing?)
I entered the living room just as the drone of the vacuum cleaner cut out.
[M]Mary[-M] was standing right in front of the closed cellar door. The rug that usually covers the gap was kicked up, and she was bending down, picking something up from the floorboards.
Hey, [M]Mary[-M]. What did you find?
She turned, startled, holding a small, strange object in her hand.
Oh! Peter. You startled me.
She walked over, holding the object out for me to see. It was a small, carved piece of dark wood, inlaid with thin, shiny copper wiring in a spiral pattern.
It didn't look like anything from this house.
Did you drop this? I found it under the rug, right by the cellar door.
I took it, turning it over in my hands. It felt heavy and strangely warm.
I’ve never seen this before in my life. It looks... old. Like an antique handle or something?
(Shit. Sloppy work. Must have slipped out of my pocket when I was sneaking back up from the lab last night.)
(Good thing you're too dense to figure it out, "daywalker".)
I frowned, turning the object over. For a second, I felt a weird, inexplicable prickle at the back of my neck. A sense of déjà vu that I couldn't place.
Maybe it's been down there for years? Just some old junk from the basement?
Perhaps. It’s very strange, though. I don't remember ever seeing it before.
She gently took it back from me.
Well, no use worrying about it. I’ll just put it in the junk drawer for now.
I watched her walk to the kitchen, then glanced back at the cellar door. It was just a door. Locked, dusty, and boring. I shrugged and turned away.
(Yeah... probably just trash.)

s2_opening_016.text: The door clicked shut. Silence rushed back into the room, filling the void [T]Tiffany[-T] had left behind.
I stood in the middle of the floor, the cool morning air hitting my skin. My heart was still hammering against my ribs like a trapped bird.
I turned back to the bed to straighten the messy sheets. My breath hitched.
There, half-buried under the pillow I had just been sitting on... a flash of delicate pink lace.
(Wait... what? I thought we were just bluffing! I didn't know they were actually there!)
(When did I...? How did I...?)
(I told you, [MC]Peter[-MC]. I provide. You just execute.)
(You were sitting on her scent the whole time. Absorbing it. Intimate, isn't it?)
My hand trembled as I snatched the silk scrap and shoved it deep into my pocket. I felt like a criminal. A pervert.
(Relax. The crime is the best part.)
(And don't worry about her coming back. She didn't run after the dog, [MC]Peter[-MC]. That was just an excuse.)
(She saw it. She judged it. And she completely lost her cool.)
(That wasn't fear. That was shock. Pure, wide-eyed bewilderment mixed with a very flushed face.)
(She’s going to be thinking about that all day. Every time she grabs a handle at the gym... she's going to remember this.)
(I... I can't believe this. I'm a liar and a thief.)
(But Red is right. She looked... stunned. Like she short-circuited.)
(I need to put on pants. Now. Before I do something else I regret.)
I wrestled my jeans on. It was a physical struggle, like trying to sheath a broadsword in a toothpick holder.
The denim was tight, unforgiving. Zipping up felt like defusing a bomb—one wrong move, and kaboom.
I grimaced. I could barely walk. Every step was a pinch. It was agony.
(Pain is just weakness leaving the body. Or sperm trying to escape. Either way, move your ass.)
(We have a breakfast to ruin and a household dynamic to destroy. [M]Mary[-M] is waiting.)
I shuffled to the door, doing the wide-legged cowboy strut of shame. It was going to be a long morning.

s2_priscilla_route_057.text: Back in the safety of my room, I collapsed onto my bed.
My mind was a whirlwind of Priscilla’s triumphant, tear-streaked face.
The taste of her lipstick was still a ghost on my skin, and the memory of her throat finally yielding around me lingered.
What the fuck is my life right now?
(It's fucking awesome, is what it is. I haven't had this much fun since… well, ever.)
(That was a masterpiece. A symphony of pride, submission, and spit.)
She’s completely obsessed. She was talking about her next 'training' before the cum was even dry on her face. This is getting out of control.
(Out of your control, maybe. It's perfectly under mine. See? I told you.)
(A little pressure, a little competition, and she crumbles into the perfect little slut.)
(She’s not just a fuck toy anymore. She's a willing student. An acolyte.)
An acolyte of what? The church of your giant dick?
(Exactly! And as her spiritual guide, it is my sacred duty to lead her to the next level of enlightenment.)
(She has conquered the oral sacrament. You know what comes next.)
I knew exactly what he was talking about. The thing he’d mentioned before. The final frontier. A cold knot of anxiety tightened in my stomach.
No. Absolutely not.
I could feel his amusement, cold and sharp in my mind.
('No'? Don't be boring. She's ready. She's begging for it, even if she doesn't know the words yet.)
Are you insane?! Did you see her? She was crying from the effort! Her jaw is probably killing her.
She could barely handle my dick in her throat, a place that's meant to stretch. And you want to try and shove it in her ass?
(That's the whole point! The struggle is what makes it hot! She wants to be pushed.)
(She wants to be broken a little, so we can build her back up into whatever we want.)
You'll tear her in half! This isn't a game, Red! That was… different. She was trying to prove something to herself.
This is just… cruel. We could actually break her, for real. Scare her off for good.
(Scare her off? Are you fucking kidding me? She’s addicted to us! To this feeling!)
(Conquering her ass is the final test of her devotion. That's when we'll truly, completely own every part of her. It’s the ultimate prize.)
I don’t care. We’re not doing it. It’s too much. I won't let you.
Find another way to "test" her. Make her do… I don’t know, something else. But not that.
I felt a wave of cold disappointment from him. He was genuinely annoyed.
(Tsk. You're getting soft. You finally get a taste of real power, and you get scared. Pathetic.)
Call it what you want. The answer is no.
(Fine. Have it your way. We'll put a pin in it… for now.)
(But don't think for a second I'm forgetting about it. That tight, perfect, unconquered little asshole is on the menu. And sooner or later, we're going to have a feast.)

Bridge_01.text: The man in the water. He hates the moonlight.
There's no one down there, Jessica. It's just the dark.
There is always someone there. We are never alone. Not even in our own minds. Isn't that right, Peter?
(She knows. How the fuck does she know?)

s2_opening_032.text: (I can't deal with this. Taksh is showing his ass in the window. The couch smells like [M]Mary[-M]. I'm going back to bed.)
I turned to the stairs.
THUMP. THUMP. THUMP.
Heavy, fast footsteps coming down from the corridor above.
(Halt.)
(It's [T]Tiffany[-T]. She sounds pissed.)
(If you go up those stairs now, your face will be at perfect crotch-height when she rounds the corner.)
(She will kick you. In the face. You will fall down the stairs and break your neck.)
(You end up back here, but dead. Stay put.)
(I'm trapped.)
(You're not trapped. You're the host of the party. And the first guest is coming down the ramp.)
(Here she comes.)
YOU!
She flew off the last step, storming into the living room like a hurricane.
She was wearing jeans and a tight t-shirt now, but her wet hair was whipping around her face. She looked ready to commit murder.
You sick freak! Do you think I didn't see you upstairs? Do you think-
She marched toward me, raising a finger to poke my chest... and then she stopped.
Dead in her tracks.
She had stepped past me to get in my face. Which meant she was now facing the large front window.
Her mouth opened to scream, but no sound came out. Her fury evaporated, replaced by pure, unadulterated confusion.
Her eyes went wide. I thought they might actually pop out of her skull.
What...
What is that?
She squinted, leaning forward slightly, as if trying to resolve a optical illusion.
Is that... a person? Or did a giant, hairy peach just fly into the glass?
(She’s processing. Give her a moment.)
(She’s confused. She thinks someone taped a shag carpet to the window.)

I’m implying that our daughter is a thoroughbred, just like her favorite horse. And thoroughbreds need to be broken in.
Don't worry your head about it, darling. I have a feeling things are about to become much more... entertaining.
(Entertaining for us, maybe. This family is a beautiful, twisted fucking mess. And we're right in the middle of it.)

s2_ending_001.text: [M]Mary[-M] had secured the latch with a thick, heavy-duty plastic zip-tie to stop us from "wasting electricity."
(Look at that little plastic fortress. She thinks a zip-tie can stop progress.)
(I can't open it. It's pulled completely tight. If I yank on it, [M]Mary[-M] will hear the metal rattling from downstairs.)
(You don't need to yank it. You just need the right leverage. Remember the souvenir you brought back from the Sterling mansion?)
I reached into my pocket and pulled out Gerda's heavy gardening multi-tool. The steel jaws of the wire cutters gleamed in the dim hallway light.
(This is a terrible idea. If [T]Tiffany[-T] finds out I did this...)
(She won't. She's going to be too distracted sweating out her body weight. Cut it.)
The thick plastic zip-tie severed instantly under the sharp steel jaws. It dropped silently to the carpet.
I opened the metal door. Inside, a row of switches and fuses hummed quietly. I found the one labeled "Zone 2 - T. Room".
(Pull it. Let's turn the Ice Queen's castle into a sauna.)
I grabbed the fuse and yanked it out. A faint, dying wheeze echoed from the vents above.
(It's done. Her room is completely cut off from the cooling system.)
(Perfect. By tonight, that room will be an oven. The trap is set. Now we just wait for the prey to get thirsty.)
I closed the panel, pocketed the tool, and walked away before anyone could see me.

UniversityWalterCabinet_03.text: Ah, Peter. Come in. Don't hover in the doorway. What can I do for you?
Hello, Dean Walter. I just wanted to drop off my elective registration forms. I didn't mean to interrupt your work.
(Look at him looking down his nose at us. I bet that chair is just as comfortable as I imagined. Ask him how much university money he embezzled to buy it. Establish dominance!)
Not an interruption at all. Place them on the edge of the desk, please.
Tell me, how are you finding the semester so far? The coursework isn't proving too overwhelming, I trust?
It's challenging, sir, but manageable. I'm just trying to stay focused and keep my grades up.
(Boring! Tell him about the real extracurricular activities we have planned. Tell him we're going to turn his pristine campus upside down.)
Glad to hear it. We pride ourselves on maintaining a rigorous academic standard here. I expect you to uphold that standard, Peter. We have no patience for slackers or troublemakers.
Absolutely, Dean Walter. You don't have to worry about me.
Excellent. I'll review these forms later. Have a productive day.

s2_map_mall_first_click.text: (The mall. It’s got the arcade and the food court. Always packed with people.)
(Packed with people means packed with opportunities. Lots of bored girls wandering around just waiting for some real excitement... Let's see what kind of trouble we can find.)
